Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
No representation for the
revisionist, though called twice.
2. Mr. Dinesh Chauhan, learned
A.G.A. for the State.
3. Mr. Veer Kunwar Singh, learnd
counsel for respondent no.2 through
Video Conferencing.
4. By means of the present
criminal revisions, the revisionists
have challenged the judgment and
order dated 30.11.2019 passed by
the learned Additional Sessions
Judge, Bageshwar, affirming the
judgment and order of conviction
and sentence dated 25.07.2019
passed by the learned Judicial
Magistrate, Bageshwar under Section
138 of the Negotiable Instruments
Act, 1881.
5. Since all the criminal revisions
arise out of the same complaint case,
involve identical parties and raise
common questions of fact and law,
they were heard together and are
being decided by this common

2026:UHC:4763
judgment.
6. The brief facts of the case are
that the respondent
no.2/complainant instituted a
complaint under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instruments Act alleging
that the revisionists had issued
certain cheques towards discharge of
their legally enforceable liability.
Upon presentation, the said cheques
were dishonoured. Thereafter, a
statutory notice under Section 138 of
the Negotiable Instruments Act was
served upon the revisionists
demanding payment of the cheque
amount, but despite receipt of the
notice, the revisionists failed to make
payment within the stipulated
period. Consequently, Complaint
Case was instituted before the
learned Judicial Magistrate,
Bageshwar. Upon appreciation of the
evidence on record, the learned
Magistrate convicted and sentenced
the revisionists under Section 138 of
the Negotiable Instruments Act vide
judgment and order dated
25.07.2019. Aggrieved thereby, the
revisionists preferred Criminal
Appeal, which also came to be
dismissed by the learned Additional
Sessions Judge, Bageshwar vide
judgment and order dated

2026:UHC:4763
30.11.2019.
7. A perusal of the order-sheet of
the present revisions reveals that the
revisionists had given an
undertaking before this Court to
liquidate the outstanding amount in
four instalments. On 24.07.2025,
learned counsel appearing for the
revisionists submitted that the first
instalment of ₹5,00,000/- would be
deposited on or before 15.10.2025
and that an affidavit disclosing such
compliance would also be filed before
this Court.
8. The report submitted by the
Registry indicates that no such
affidavit has been filed by the
revisionists. Learned counsel for
respondent no.2 has further
submitted that the revisionists have
failed to comply with the undertaking
furnished before this Court and have
not paid any amount whatsoever to
respondent no.2.
9. Today, none appears on behalf
of the revisionists.
10. Having heard learned counsel
for respondent no.2, perused the
material available on record and
considered the concurrent findings
recorded by the courts below, this
Court does not find any jurisdictional
error, illegality, perversity or material

2026:UHC:4763
irregularity in the impugned
judgments warranting interference in
exercise of revisional jurisdiction.
11. The revisionists have not only
failed to demonstrate any infirmity in
the judgments of the courts below
but have also failed to comply with
the undertaking given before this
Court regarding payment of the
cheque amount.
12. Accordingly, all the criminal
revisions fail and are hereby
dismissed. The judgments and
orders dated 25.07.2019 passed by
the learned Judicial Magistrate,
Bageshwar and dated 30.11.2019
passed by the learned Additional
Sessions Judge, Bageshwar are
affirmed.
13. No order as to costs.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 11.06.2026 Mamta
